about:
Custom Manufacturing Services, Inc. (CMS) and East River Metals, Inc. (ERM) operate from three facilities in Princeton, West Virginia, and Rocky Gap, Virginia. The business traces its roots to 1979 when Bob Graf founded East River Metals to produce metal enclosures for its sister company, American Mine Research. In 1995, Graf established Custom Manufacturing Services to combine ERM's sheet metal expertise with American Mine Research's electro-mechanical assembly capabilities. Today, the company remains family-led under president David Graf.

The two entities together provide precision sheet metal fabrication, turnkey electro-mechanical assembly, and powder and wet spray coating. Core processes include laser cutting, forming, welding, hardware insertion, and outsourced plating. The combined footprint spans more than 155,000 square feet of manufacturing, office, and warehouse space across the two states.

Customers span mining, aerospace and defense, electronics, food processing, industrial machinery, and oil and gas. Named clients include American Mine Research, Moog, Pascor Atlantic, Forensic Computers, JBS, Caron, and Smyth Co. Machine.

The company emphasizes complete in-house control over fabrication, assembly, and finishing to deliver quick turnarounds and consistent quality. Its quality policy targets exceeding customer expectations, supported by ISO 9001:2015 certification and statistical process controls such as CpK studies and FMEA.

name: Custom Metal Products
old_description: Without having to buy and maintain a variety of steel, copper, aluminum, etc, in  inventory.
about:
Custom Metal Products operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it was established in 1988 after Steve and Cheryl Ryan purchased the business from a previous father‑son ownership. The Ryans built the company while Steve worked as a hotshot driver, and their son Keith later learned the trade before teaching Alan Cofran to run the operation in 1998. Today the business continues as a family‑owned enterprise, with Cofran at the helm alongside his son A.J. and longtime associate Josh, maintaining the legacy on Vassar Place Northeast.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, cutting and bending mild steel from 29‑gauge to 16‑gauge and stainless steel up to 22‑gauge. A Berridge T‑panel machine adds radius‑forming capability for Berridge‑brand panels. The company also supplies sheet metal screws and clips and handles trim work in galvanized, copper and aluminum.

Customers range from roofing and HVAC contractors to general construction firms needing architectural metal components, though the company does not publish a formal industry list. Its flexibility in accepting customer‑supplied material and its willingness to work early, late or weekend hours by arrangement make it a practical extension of a client’s own fabrication capacity.

The business was founded to give other companies a “metal shop” without the overhead of plant space, capital equipment, trained personnel or material inventory—a positioning it still emphasizes today.

about:
Custom Packaging House operates from Casper, Wyoming, where it provides custom printed boxes, Mylar pouches, and wholesale packaging solutions. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure, and no founders are named in its materials.

The company manufactures custom packaging boxes and printed Mylar bags using screen, digital, offset, lithography, and flexography printing processes, with CMYK and PMS color options. Finishing capabilities include spot UV, matte and gloss coatings, embossing, debossing, foiling, die-cutting, and raised ink. The company reports 500-plus box styles, 10,000-plus orders delivered, and service across 50-plus industries, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Customers span food and beverage, apparel, cosmetics, retail, vape, nutraceuticals, toys and collectibles, personal care, confectionery, and gift markets. The company serves brands of all sizes, offering wholesale quantities with low minimums and free design support.

Custom Packaging House states its mission is to build long-term client relationships through quality, integrity, commitment, and responsibility. Its vision is to attain a reputable position in the packaging industry by delivering superior, visually appealing, and innovative custom boxes. Stated differentiators include free design support with 3D mockups, free samples on demand, eco-friendly material options, 24-hour quote response, 8–10 day dispatch, free shipping, and a 30% launch discount.

Custom Packaging Services operates from Richmond, Virginia. The founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company provides a range of packaging and logistics services, including custom corrugated box design and assembly, custom wooden crate and pallet manufacturing, shrink wrapping, shrink sleeving, registered bundling, foil and card blistering, RF clamshell packaging, point-of-purchase displays, package gluing, product repackaging, relabeling, package design, packout services, kitting and assembly, manual hand assembly, fulfillment, and warehousing. They manufacture custom wooden crates and pallets built to shipment specifications and specialize in shrink wrapping retail packages and products.

Custom Packaging Services partners with businesses to scale operations in production, storage, and handling or shipping. The company emphasizes flexibility and reliability, promoting "Custom Orders • Low Minimums • Fast Turn-Around Times" and describing itself as "LARGE ENOUGH TO BE RELIABLE • SMALL ENOUGH TO BE FLEXIBLE." It cites production-line accuracy as a source of its reputation for excellence.

name: Custom Sheet Metal of Louisiana
old_description: In addition to custom fabrication of sheet metal products, we provide a number of other services for the convenience of our customers.
about:
Custom Sheet Metal of Louisiana operates from Lafayette, Louisiana. The business was acquired in 2011 by Chad Duhon, who had worked at the shop since 1995 and served as foreman before taking ownership. Duhon brought two decades of sheet metal experience, including earlier work at Butcher Air Conditioning. In 2011, Jared Breaux joined as co-owner and partner; Breaux had previously worked at the company from 2002 to 2005 and later ran gutter and patio cover ventures before returning. Breaux also served in the U.S. Army after studying at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, offering welding, plasma cutting, and forming for a range of products including awnings, Cajun microwaves, restaurant hood exhausts, HVAC ductwork, fan shrouds, drain pans, flashing, louvers, chimney caps, and seamless gutters in half-round and K-style profiles. Beyond fabrication, the company provides installation of its own products and of prefabricated restaurant-grade exhaust hoods, gutter cleaning and guard installation, AC ductwork maintenance with custom replacement parts, and sales of metal panels for patios, siding, and other construction uses.

Customers span residential homeowners, commercial contractors, and restaurant operators throughout the Lafayette area. The company’s ductwork and gutter services target HVAC and building maintenance markets, while its metal panel sales serve patio and siding construction projects. Restaurant clients rely on the firm for code-compliant exhaust hood installation.

The founders emphasize hands-on oversight: Duhon manages shop operations and estimating, while Breaux handles job scheduling, on-site supervision, and customer relationships. Their combined background in sheet metal, gutter systems, and industrial supply chains informs the company’s focus on craftsmanship and responsive service.

name: Custom Steel Manufacturing
old_description: Metal Fabrication::: We have the biggest machines in the Midwest
about:
Custom Steel Manufacturing, Inc. operates from Belton, Missouri, where it runs a metal fabrication shop focused on heavy-capacity processing. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure in its public materials.

The shop offers shearing up to 40 feet, bending up to 36 feet, seam welding up to 20 feet, plate rolling up to 20 feet, plasma cutting on a 4-foot by unlimited-length table, and punching up to 4 inches. It works with carbon steel, A588, AR400, stainless steel, C276, titanium, and aluminum in forms including plate, angle, bar, sheet, pipe, channel, and beam. Equipment includes a Do-All 305 automatic-feed horizontal production band saw and multiple additional band saws. The company accepts custom prototypes, short runs, and large fabrication projects.

Custom Steel Manufacturing serves customers across industries that require heavy metal fabrication, though specific sectors are not listed on its site. Typical engagements involve one-off prototypes, limited production runs, and large-scale structural projects.

The company emphasizes its machine capacity, stating it owns the "biggest, most powerful machines in the Midwest" and aims to "make the impossible possible" for challenging fabrication jobs.

name: Cyril's Foods
old_description: Little pops of joy made for celebrations, snacking, and everyday indulgence.
about:
Cyril's Foods operates from Fort Lauderdale, Florida. The company's founding year and ownership details are not publicly disclosed. It began as an innovative bakery company focused on creating distinctive products for foodservice channels.

The company produces three core product lines: cake pops made with 100% real chocolate and shaped into consistent spheres; gourmet toaster pastries featuring flaky crusts, indulgent fillings, and delicate icing; and cheesy egg & potato waffles composed of equal parts shredded potatoes, cheddar cheese, and eggs, with chives. The waffles are marketed as gluten-free, low-carb, and keto-friendly. Production includes foodservice bulk packing and foodservice packing capabilities.

Cyril's Foods supplies coffee shops, convenience stores, and in-store bakeries. Its cake pops have been adopted by a 600-unit coffee chain where the Birthday Cake flavor became a top seller, and by a 60-unit coffee chain that called the launch the most successful product introduction in its history.

The company emphasizes creativity and consumer appeal to help customers differentiate their assortments. Its cake pops are noted for using only real chocolate and achieving a perfectly round shape, while its waffles target health-conscious consumers with gluten-free and keto attributes.
